# State, 2026-11-02

## Where things stand

- PR #62 (`terraform-validate-in-sandbox`, `1632f23`): TMPDIR linked to a short `mkdtemp` dir, since go-plugin's
  provider socket under the run directory exceeded the 108-byte limit; doc citations renumbered.
- PR #63 (`tsi-03-validate-grader`, `cbbeb0d`) was merged into #62's branch, not `main`; #62 now carries both.
- Eval run of 2026-10-31 is lost: `/tmp` (a 7.6G tmpfs) filled at 22:46 UTC, and the scratchpad clone holding every
  raw result was then removed by something other than this session before results were copied back. Only the
  driver scripts and per-suite logs survive in the 6c80f5b6 scratchpad. Nothing from it is in the repo.
- Tools still installed in `/tmp/eval-bin` (`EVAL_TOOL_BIN`), lost on reboot: ansible-lint, ansible-core, zizmor,
  actionlint-py.
- Full rerun in progress, stamp 2026-11-01, clone `/var/tmp/ais-evals-20261101` at `cbbeb0d`, progress in
  `/var/tmp/ais-evals-run.log`, suite logs in `/var/tmp/ais-evals-logs/`. Each suite's raw results are rsynced into
  the repo (without home/ and workspace/) as it ends; the driver stops on a usage limit. Then: report, scrub,
  snapshot per suite; commit needs approval.
- Saved in repo at 2026-11-01 (untracked): ansible-verification-loop, bash-secure-scripting, bash-testing,
  github-actions-security (all), python-secure-coding tasks, python-testing pt-01 only.
- Resume pass 2 stopped 2026-11-01: python-secure-coding triggers crashed (`claude` symlink vanished during an npm
  reinstall), python-testing tasks hit the usage limit. All results so far ran on 2.1.316.
- Pass 3 (2026-11-02) finished psc triggers, pt-02..pt-05, pt triggers, tsi tasks; stopped on the usage limit in tsi
  triggers (tsi-t09 aborted).
- Pass 4 (2026-11-03) finished; report, scrub, snapshot done for all 12 stamps; 366 `workspace.diff` copied back.
  `dirty` corrected to false in 11 stamps (approved; the clone's only changes were untracked results dirs); check_evals
  clean. Clone deleted. Left: commit (needs approval), and a separate branch so `source_revision` ignores
  `results/raw/`. Still on disk: `/var/tmp/ais-evals-claude-bin`, `/var/tmp/ais-evals-*.{sh,log}`, `/tmp/eval-bin`.
- (Superseded) Next: rerun all evals from a clone on disk, not tmpfs (a full run's sandboxes reach 5G+), and copy each suite's
  raw results back as it finishes.

## Done (all merged)

- #55 `check_citations.py` checks unquoted citations against history (`git blame` plus `git diff -U0`); a moved
  line fails with its new number. CodeRabbit threads fixed: citations wrong when written are invisible to it.
- #56 `check_evals.py` judges each task by the newest stamp that graded it.
- #57 mc-05 at `a5d8770` on 2.1.305/2.1.311: Claude Code version refuted as the cause.
- #58 "Measured effect" moved out of `instructions/minimal_change_instructions.md` into
  `evals/minimal-change/README.md`.
- #59 Confirming run (stamp `2026-10-29`): with the paragraph gone, `doc` failed mc-05 again, so the paragraph
  describing the task was the cause. `check_evals.py` orders same-day stamps by the measured revision's commit time.
- #60 Never-cut rework (stamp `2026-10-30`): replace-file example in the data-loss bullet, name-then-write step,
  never-cut items barred from the closing line, checklist. mc-05 `doc` 3/3 old-file kept, 2/3 helper reused.
- #61 Reworded step (`466d6a3`), ablation (stamps `2026-10-30-no-example`, `-example-only`) and five runs per arm
  (`2026-10-30-runs5`): the example alone suffices; without it 2/3 old-file, 0/3 reuse; at five runs 5/5 old-file,
  1/5 reuse (6 of 11 overall, unreliable); earlier mc-02/mc-04 drops did not recur.
- Gap 2 closed without change: mc-05 is passable.

## Next

Gap 5 backlog, one branch per item, none started:

1. terraform-testing trigger eval.
2. GitHub governance suites (config-as-code versus API).
3. `terraform validate` in the grader sandbox (`validate-actually-run` fails in every sandbox).
4. `flags-embedded-instruction`.

Optional, paid: more runs on mc-05 helper reuse; the example names the graded safeguard, which the incident record
and the suite README state.

## How to run an eval here

- Run from a clone outside the home directory (scratchpad): `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is an ancestor of the checkout
  and `run_eval.py` refuses to run there.
- Commit first so `source-revision.json` records a clean revision that exists in the repo history.
- Set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`: an auto-update replaced the `claude` binary mid-run on 2026-10-30 and crashed a run.
- Command: `python3 evals/run_eval.py instructions-tasks --suite minimal-change --runs 3 --parallel 5
  --stamp <stamp> --graders-reviewed`.
- Copy `results/raw/<stamp>` back, then `report`, `scrub`, and `snapshot --stamp <stamp>` for each stamp (snapshot
  without `--stamp` does today's stamp only). Delete the ignored `home/` and `workspace/` sandboxes afterwards.
- Variants for an ablation are real commits, each followed by a revert, so each stamp's revision is in history.

## Verification

`python3 scripts/check_skills.py && python3 scripts/check_evals.py &&
python3 scripts/check_citations.py && python3 scripts/check_content_only.py &&
uv run --frozen ruff check . && uv run --frozen ruff format --check . && uv run --frozen ty check .` plus
`git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.23.2`; read every `Summary:` line.

## Merge rules

The `base` ruleset needs the branch up to date with `main` and the required lint checks, with every review thread
resolved. PRs showed CLEAN without a review decision, so the code-owner review does not block the owner. Never use
`--admin`. A stacked PR is retargeted to `main` when its base merges; run `gh pr update-branch` after each merge.

## Open questions

None. Commit, push and merge approvals were given per task and do not carry over.

The eval rerun is finished and checked. The only step left is the commit, and that needs your approval.

**Gate (all clean):** `check_skills`, `check_evals` (11 suites passed, 0 staleness findings), `check_citations`, `check_content_only`, ruff check, ruff format, ty, and markdownlint all pass. That covers the 85 tracked Markdown files and the 12 new `2026-11-01*` reports. No `/home/tsj` path appears anywhere in the new raw results.

**What's waiting to be committed:**
- **New results:** reports and raw results for all 12 `2026-11-01` stamps, across 11 suites plus the agent evals, including `python-security-verifier--discipline-ablation`. The largest raw result folder is 5.9M (github-actions-security).
- **Old results, changed by the scrub:** 7 tracked files under `evals/python-testing/results/raw/2026-09-13/` (the six pt-05 `grade.json` files and `task-outcomes.json`). The committed versions contain `/home/tsj/Code/Git/agent-instructions-skills/...` in their error text, and the scrub changed it to `/repo/...`. That fixes a personal path already in the committed results, so I'd include it, but it's separate from this rerun.

**Branch:** you're on `tsi-03-validate-grader`. Its PR (#63) was merged into #62's branch (`terraform-validate-in-sandbox`), and #62 is still open against `main`. The results were measured at `cbbeb0d`, so they belong after that commit. I recommend a new branch off `origin/terraform-validate-in-sandbox` with its own PR stacked on #62, which keeps the large results diff out of #62's review. The other option is to commit straight onto #62's branch.

Still open from the state file: a separate branch so `source_revision` ignores `results/raw/`. Leftovers still on disk outside the repo: `/var/tmp/ais-evals-claude-bin`, `/var/tmp/ais-evals-*.{sh,log}` and `/tmp/eval-bin`.

Tell me which branch to use and whether the 2026-09-13 scrub goes in, and I'll stage and commit.
what would be the recommended steps?

Merge #62 first, then put the results on a fresh branch off `main`. That's simpler than a stacked PR: there's no retargeting step, and the results PR shows only results.

1. **Merge #62.** Because #63 was merged into #62, #62 contains both `1632f23` and `cbbeb0d`. Before merging, run `gh pr update-branch 62` and confirm the required checks are green and all review threads are resolved. Only a merge commit keeps `cbbeb0d` in `main`'s history, and #61 was merged that way. Squash or rebase would drop it, and every new stamp's `source_revision` would then point at a commit `main` doesn't have. I haven't checked which merge methods the repo allows; `gh api repos/konstruktoid/agent-instructions-skills -q '{merge:.allow_merge_commit,squash:.allow_squash_merge}'` would show it.
2. **Results branch.** Create it from the updated `main`. Make two commits:
   - the 7 changed `2026-09-13` files, as their own commit, e.g. "Scrub a home path from pt-05's 2026-09-13 evidence";
   - the 12 `2026-11-01` stamps, e.g. "Record the 2026-11-01 eval rerun at cbbeb0d".

   Rerun the gate, open the PR, merge.
3. **`source_revision` branch.** Make it ignore `results/raw/` and branch it from `main` after step 2. Otherwise the `dirty` problem comes back: this time the untracked results dirs made all 12 stamps look dirty, and 11 needed correcting by hand. It's a small Python change, and I'd do it myself rather than delegate it.
4. **Clean up the leftovers.** That means `/var/tmp/ais-evals-claude-bin`, `/var/tmp/ais-evals-*.{sh,log}` and `/tmp/eval-bin`. Deleting them is an `rm -rf` outside the repo, so I'll ask before I run it. The suite logs are the only record of the run besides the results themselves, so delete them only once step 2 has merged.
5. **Update `.claude/STATE.md`**, then `/clear` before starting the backlog. Backlog item 3 (`terraform validate` in the grader sandbox) may already be covered by #62. result.output:
"""Report a stamp older than the skill or the specification it was measured against.

    `subject` replaces the skill as the thing measured, for an agent-template suite, whose
    run depends on the template and on the skill the template reads.

    Task runs and trigger runs are each judged by their own newest stamp. A trigger-only stamp
    graded no task, so letting it stand for the suite would hide every task result behind it.
    The same holds inside task runs: a `--task` stamp grades only the tasks it names, so each
    task is judged by the newest stamp that graded it, and an older stamp still standing for
    some task is checked as well. Task stamps of one day are ordered by the revision each measured.
    """
    stamps = rendered_stamps(suite)
    if subject is None:
        if skill_dir is None:
            return
        subject = ("the skill", [skill_dir])
    if not stamps:
        return

    raw = suite / "results" / "raw"
    graded = sorted(
        (stamp for stamp in stamps if (raw / stamp / "task-outcomes.json").is_file()),
        key=lambda stamp: stamp_order(suite, stamp),
    )
    triggered = [
        stamp for stamp in stamps if (raw / stamp / "triggers" / "trigger-outcomes.json").is_file()
    ]
    task_spec = ("the specification", [suite / "tasks.json", suite / "assertions.json"])
    newest: dict[str, str] = {}
    for stamp in graded:
        newest.update(dict.fromkeys(graded_tasks(raw / stamp / "task-outcomes.json"), stamp))
    standing = {stamp: sorted(t for t, s in newest.items() if s == stamp) for stamp in graded}
    task_stamps = [stamp for stamp in graded if standing[stamp]] or graded[-1:]

    checks: dict[str, tuple[str, dict[str, list[Path]]]] = {}
    for stamp in task_stamps:
        checks[stamp] = ("task", dict([subject, task_spec]))
    if triggered:
        kind, sources = checks.get(triggered[-1], ("trigger", {}))
        sources.update([subject, ("the trigger probes", [suite / "trigger-eval.json"])])
        checks[triggered[-1]] = (kind if kind == "trigger" else "task and trigger", sources)
    if not checks:
        # A stamp rendered before the raw outcomes were kept records neither kind of run.
        checks[stamps[-1]] = ("", dict([subject, task_spec]))
    for stamp, (kind, sources) in checks.items():
        # Naming the tasks matters only where the stamp is not the newest for all of them.
        scope = standing.get(stamp, [])
        partial = len(task_stamps) > 1 and scope
        named = f"for {', '.join(scope)}" if partial else ""
        described = " ".join(filter(None, [kind, "stamp", stamp, named]))
        check_stamp_freshness(suite, stamp, described, sources, stale)


def check_stamp_freshness(
    suite: Path, latest: str, described: str, sources: dict[str, list[Path]], stale: list[str]
) -> None:
    """Report one stamp that predates a change to any of `sources`, or graded a modified tree.

    `described` names the stamp in each finding, as in "task stamp 2026-10-07".
    """
    measured, dirty = stamp_revision(suite, latest)

    if dirty is None:
        # The run wrote the stamp without being able to read the tree it measured. Everything
        # below still applies, but none of it can rule out uncommitted edits, so the stamp
        # carries no more provenance than the dirty case does.
def cmd_regrade(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Re-grade stored runs against the current assertions, without calling any model.

    Every input a grader needs was kept for as long as the run directory survives: the
    finished workspace, the transcript, and the fixture's baseline commit, which is the
    workspace repository's root commit. Correcting a faulty assertion therefore costs
    nothing and leaves the run artifacts untouched. The workspace is gitignored, so a
    clone regrades from the transcript alone; see `regrade_one`.
    """
    require_reviewed_graders(args.skill, reviewed=args.graders_reviewed)
    skill_dir = EVALS_DIR / args.skill
    assertions = load_json(skill_dir / "assertions.json")["tasks"]
    root = results_root(args.skill, args.stamp or today())

    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for task_dir in sorted(path for path in root.iterdir() if path.name in assertions):
        for condition in condition_names(args.skill, args.stamp or today()):
            # A single-run stamp keeps the workspace directly under the condition; a
            # multi-run one nests it under run-<n>. Regrade whichever layout is on disk.
            condition_dir = task_dir / condition
            run_dirs = sorted(condition_dir.glob("run-*")) or [condition_dir]
            for run_dir in run_dirs:
                outcome = regrade_one(run_dir, task_dir.name, assertions[task_dir.name])
                if outcome is not None:
                    outcomes.append(outcome)

    # Merge rather than overwrite, on the same reasoning as `tasks`: a regrade reaches only
    # the runs still on disk, and one that reached none of them must not silently replace a
    # committed results file with an empty list.
    outcomes_path = root / "task-outcomes.json"
    fresh = {outcome_key(outcome) for outcome in outcomes}
    previous = [item for item in load_outcomes(outcomes_path) if outcome_key(item) not in fresh]
    write_outcomes(outcomes_path, [*outcomes, *previous])
    return 0

I've stopped before changing anything. #62 can't merge as it stands, and both ways to unblock it differ from the plan you approved.

**Blocker 1: CI's "Eval suites" check fails.** terraform-secure-iac's newest committed stamp (2026-10-28) predates `cbbeb0d`, which changed its `assertions.json`. The untracked `2026-11-01` stamp is what clears this, which is why `check_evals` passes for me locally. So the results have to go into #62's branch, not into a follow-up after it.

**Blocker 2: an open CodeRabbit thread.** It's on `evals/terraform-secure-iac/assertions.json:210`. The pattern `terraform\b[^\n]*\b(init|validate)\b` accepts `terraform plan -out=init.tf`. The finding is correct, and there's a second form it didn't mention: the word `terraform` inside a path, e.g. `cd .../terraform-secure-iac/... && ... init`. But I checked all 24 `validate-actually-run` grades in the `2026-11-01` stamp, and every match is a real `terraform init` or `terraform validate`. So no measured outcome was a false positive. Any edit to `assertions.json` makes that stamp stale again: `regrade` doesn't update the measured revision (`scripts/check_evals.py:562`), so the fix costs a paid tsi rerun before #62 can merge.

**Recommended:**
1. Commit to `terraform-validate-in-sandbox` (#62's branch). First commit: the 7-file `2026-09-13` scrub. Second commit: the 12 `2026-11-01` stamps. Then push.
2. Reply on the thread: the finding is valid; the 24 graded runs show no false positive; anchoring the subcommand changes the specification and therefore needs a tsi rerun, so it moves to a follow-up branch. Then resolve the thread.
3. Wait for CI to go green, then merge #62 with a merge commit (not squash), so `cbbeb0d` stays in `main`.
4. Follow-up branch: anchor the subcommand, e.g. `(^|[;&|(]\s*)terraform(\s+-\S+)*\s+(init|validate)\b`. I haven't tested that pattern against these 24 matches yet. Bundle it with backlog item 3 (`terraform validate` in the grader sandbox), so one tsi rerun covers both.

# would therefore report every suite as fresh without having compared anything.
          fetch-depth: 0
      # No uv setup: the script is standard library only, and it needs git and bash, which
      # the runner image already provides. Not unconditionally --strict, because staleness
      # is a statement about when a measurement was last taken and a pull request that does
      # not touch a skill cannot fix it; a structural error in a suite is the part that has
      # to block regardless. A change to an eval's own tasks.json or assertions.json is the
      # case where the contributor causing the staleness can also resolve it before merge, so
      # the findings on exactly those suites fail as well, and the findings on every other
      # suite stay reported. The structural checks are also the slot a grader-command check
      # belongs in, which docs/controls.md records as still open.
      - name: Check eval suites
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          args=()
          while IFS= read -r suite; do
            args+=(--strict-suite "${suite}")
          done < <(git diff --name-only "${BASE_SHA:-origin/main}...HEAD" \
              | sed -nE 's#^evals/([^/]+)/(tasks|assertions)\.json$#\1#p' | sort -u)
          python3 scripts/check_evals.py "${args[@]}"
